sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ sahadevaḥ pipāsitaḥ apibac chītalaṃ toyaṃ pītvā ca nipapāta ha
english: Ignoring that warning, Sahadeva, overcome by thirst, drank the cool water — and having drunk, he fell down dead.

sanskrit: athābravīt sa vijayaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātarau te ciragatau bībhatso śatrukarśana tau caivānaya bhadraṃ te pānīyaṃ ca tvam ānaya
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, spoke to Vijaya: "Your two brothers have been gone a long time, O Bībhatsu, crusher of foes — bring them back, blessings on you, and bring water as well."

sanskrit: evam ukto guḍākeśaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ āmuktakhaḍgo medhāvī tat saraḥ pratyapadyata
english: Thus addressed, the wise Guḍākeśa took up his bow with arrows, girded his sword, and set out toward that lake.

sanskrit: yataḥ puruṣaśārdūlau pānīyaharaṇe gatau tau dadarśa hatau tatra bhrātarau śvetavāhanaḥ
english: Where those two tiger-men had gone to fetch water, there Śvetavāhana saw his two brothers lying slain.

sanskrit: prasuptāv iva tau dṛṣṭvā narasiṃhaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ dhanur udyamya kaunteyo vyalokayata tad vanam
english: Seeing them as if asleep, that lion among men was filled with deep grief; the son of Kuntī raised his bow and scanned the forest all around.

sanskrit: nāpaśyat tatra kiṃ cit sa bhūtaṃ tasmin mahāvane savyasācī tataḥ śrāntaḥ pānīyaṃ so 'bhyadhāvata
english: He saw no creature anywhere in that great forest; then Savyasācī, exhausted, rushed toward the water.

sanskrit: abhidhāvaṃs tato vācam antarikṣāt sa śuśruve kim āsīd asi pānīyaṃ naitac chakyaṃ balāt tvayā
english: As he rushed forward he heard a voice from the sky: "Why this haste? This water cannot be taken by force by you."

sanskrit: kaunteya yadi vai praśnān mayoktān pratipatsyase tataḥ pāsyasi pānīyaṃ hariṣyasi ca bhārata
english: "O son of Kuntī, if you answer the questions I put to you, then you shall drink the water and carry it away, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: vāritas tv abravīt pārtho dṛśyamāno nivāraya yāvad bāṇair vinirbhinnaḥ punar naivaṃ vadiṣyasi
english: Stopped thus, Pārtha replied: "Show yourself and stop me — until you are pierced through by my arrows you will not speak so again."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ pārthaḥ śarair astrānumantritaiḥ vavarṣa tāṃ diśaṃ kṛtsnāṃ śabdavedhaṃ ca darśayan
english: Having spoken thus, Pārtha then poured a rain of arrows consecrated with weapon-spells upon that entire quarter, displaying his skill of hitting by sound.

sanskrit: karṇinālīkanārācān utsṛjan bharatarṣabha anekair iṣusaṃghātair antarikṣaṃ vavarṣa ha
english: Releasing kārṇī, nālīka, and iron-headed arrows, O bull of the Bharatas, he showered the sky with many volleys of shafts.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ vighātena te pārtha praśnān uktvā tataḥ piba anuktvā tu tataḥ praśnān pītvaiva na bhaviṣyasi
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the use of this resistance, O Pārtha? Answer the questions first, then drink — if you drink without answering the questions you shall be no more."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa tv amoghān iṣūn muktvā tṛṣṇayābhiprapīḍitaḥ avijñāyaiva tān praśnān pītvaiva nipapāta ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But he, having released his unerring arrows, tormented by thirst, without answering those questions drank and fell down dead.

sanskrit: athābravīd bhīmasenaṃ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca bībhatsuś cāparājitaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, spoke to Bhīmasena: "Nakula, Sahadeva, and undefeated Bībhatsu —

sanskrit: ciraṃ gatās toyahetor na cāgacchanti bhārata tāṃś caivānaya bhadraṃ te pānīyaṃ ca tvam ānaya
english: — have long since gone for water and do not return, O Bhārata. Bring them back, blessings on you, and bring water yourself as well."

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tathety uktvā tāṃ diśaṃ pratyapadyata yatra te puruṣavyāghrā bhrātaro 'sya nipātitāḥ
english: Bhīmasena agreed and set out in that direction where those tiger-men, his brothers, had been struck down.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā duḥkhito bhīmas tṛṣayā ca prapīḍitaḥ amanyata mahābāhuḥ karma tad yakṣarakṣasām sa cintayām āsa tadā yoddhavyaṃ dhruvam adya me
english: Seeing them, mighty-armed Bhīma was filled with grief and tormented by thirst; he concluded that this was the deed of yakṣas or rākṣasas, and he thought: "Today I must certainly fight."

sanskrit: pāsyāmi tāvat pānīyam iti pārtho vṛkodaraḥ tato 'bhyadhāvat pānīyaṃ pipāsuḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: "I shall drink the water first," thought Pārtha Vṛkodara, and that bull among men rushed toward the water, overcome by thirst.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ praśnān uktvā tu kaunteya tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: The yakṣa said: "Do not act rashly, dear one — this is my prior possession. Answer the questions first, O son of Kuntī, then drink and take water away."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tato bhīmo yakṣeṇāmitatejasā avijñāyaiva tān praśnān pītvaiva nipapāta ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the yakṣa of boundless energy, Bhīma, without answering those questions, drank — and fell down dead.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntīsuto rājā vicintya puruṣarṣabhaḥ samutthāya mahābāhur dahyamānena cetasā
english: Then the king, son of Kuntī, that bull among men, reflected deeply; the mighty-armed one rose up with a burning heart.

sanskrit: apetajananirghoṣaṃ praviveśa mahāvanam rurubhiś ca varāhaiś ca pakṣibhiś ca niṣevitam
english: He entered the great forest, empty of human sounds, inhabited by spotted deer, boars, and birds.

sanskrit: nīlabhāsvaravarṇaiś ca pādapair upaśobhitam bhramarair upagītaṃ ca pakṣibhiś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: The forest was adorned with trees of dark lustrous hues and was resonant with the humming of bees and the calls of birds — so went that man of great glory.

sanskrit: sa gacchan kānane tasmin hemajālapariṣkṛtam dadarśa tat saraḥ śrīmān viśvakarmakṛtaṃ yathā
english: As he walked through that forest, the glorious one saw that lake, adorned with a net of golden lotuses, looking as if made by Viśvakarman himself.

sanskrit: upetaṃ nalinījālaiḥ sindhuvāraiś ca vetasaiḥ ketakaiḥ karavīraiś ca pippalaiś caiva saṃvṛtam śramārtas tad upāgamya saro dṛṣṭvātha vismitaḥ
english: Filled with clusters of lotuses, bordered by sindhuvāra shrubs, reeds, ketaka flowers, oleanders, and pipal trees — weary from his exertions he approached that lake and stood there, astonished at the sight.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa dadarśa hatān bhrātṝṃl lokapālān iva cyutān yugānte samanuprāpte śakrapratimagauravān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He saw his brothers lying slain — like the world-guardians fallen when the end of an age arrives — men whose dignity rivalled that of Śakra himself.

sanskrit: viprakīrṇadhanurbāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā nihatam arjunam bhīmasenaṃ yamau cobhau nirviceṣṭān gatāyuṣaḥ
english: He saw Arjuna with his bow and arrows scattered, slain; Bhīmasena and both twins lying motionless, their lives departed.

sanskrit: sa dīrgham uṣṇaṃ niḥśvasya śokabāṣpapariplutaḥ buddhyā vicintayām āsa vīrāḥ kena nipātitāḥ
english: He breathed a long, hot sigh, flooded with tears of grief, and reflected in his mind: "By whom have these heroes been struck down?"

sanskrit: naiṣāṃ śastraprahāro 'sti padaṃ nehāsti kasya cit bhūtaṃ mahad idaṃ manye bhrātaro yena me hatāḥ ekāgraṃ cintayiṣyāmi pītvā vetsyāmi vā jalam
english: "There is no weapon-wound on them, nor is there any footprint here of anyone. I believe it is some great being by which my brothers have been slain. I will concentrate my mind — I will drink the water, or I will find out."

sanskrit: syāt tu duryodhanenedam upāṃśuvihitaṃ kṛtam gāndhārarājaracitaṃ satataṃ jihmabuddhinā
english: "Or this might be the secret work of Duryodhana, contrived by the king of Gāndhāra, that crooked-minded one who schemes without ceasing."

sanskrit: yasya kāryam akāryaṃ vā samam eva bhavaty uta kas tasya viśvased vīro durmater akṛtātmanaḥ
english: "For him, right action and wrong action are equally the same — what hero could trust that evil-minded, undisciplined soul?"

sanskrit: atha vā puruṣair gūḍhaiḥ prayogo 'yaṃ durātmanaḥ bhaved iti mahābāhur bahudhā samacintayat
english: "Or perhaps this is the doing of that wicked one through agents working in secret," thought the mighty-armed one, turning it over many times in his mind.

sanskrit: tasyāsīn na viṣeṇedam udakaṃ dūṣitaṃ yathā mukhavarṇāḥ prasannā me bhrātṝṇām ity acintayat
english: "Yet the water does not appear to be poisoned, for the complexions of my brothers' faces are serene," he reflected.

sanskrit: ekaikaśaś caughabalān imān puruṣasattamān ko 'nyaḥ pratisamāseta kālāntakayamād ṛte
english: "Who other than Yama at the end of an age could individually match these best of men, each one of whom possesses the strength of a flood?"

sanskrit: etenādhyavasāyena tat toyam avagāḍhavān gāhamānaś ca tat toyam antarikṣāt sa śuśruve
english: With this resolution he waded into that water — and as he was wading in, he heard a voice from the sky.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca ahaṃ bakaḥ śaivalamatsyabhakṣo; mayā nītāḥ pretavaśaṃ tavānujāḥ tvaṃ pañcamo bhavitā rājaputra; na cet praśnān pṛcchato vyākaroṣi
english: The yakṣa said: "I am a heron, a feeder on water-weeds and fish. It is by me that your younger brothers have been sent to the realm of the dead. You shall be the fifth, O prince — unless you answer my questions."

sanskrit: mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ praśnān uktvā tu kaunteya tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: "Do not act rashly, dear one — this is my prior possession. Answer the questions first, O son of Kuntī, then drink and take water away."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rudrāṇāṃ vā vasūnāṃ vā marutāṃ vā pradhānabhāk pṛcchāmi ko bhavān devo naitac chakuninā kṛtam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Are you foremost among the Rudras, the Vasus, or the Maruts? I ask — who are you, O god? This was not done by Śakuni."

sanskrit: himavān pāriyātraś ca vindhyo malaya eva ca catvāraḥ parvatāḥ kena pātitā bhuvi tejasā
english: "Himavān, Pāriyātra, Vindhya, and Malaya — these four great mountains, by whose energy were they brought low to the earth?"

sanskrit: atīva te mahat karma kṛtaṃ balavatāṃ vara yan na devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ viṣaheran mahāyuddhe kṛtaṃ te tan mahādbhutam
english: "Truly great is the deed you have done, O best of the mighty — that which gods, gandharvas, asuras, and rākṣasas together could not endure in great battle: what you have done is a supreme wonder."

sanskrit: na te jānāmi yat kāryaṃ nābhijānāmi kāṅkṣitam kautūhalaṃ mahaj jātaṃ sādhvasaṃ cāgataṃ mama
english: "I do not know what you want, nor do I recognize your wish; great curiosity has arisen in me, and awe has come upon me."

sanskrit: yenāsmy udvignahṛdayaḥ samutpannaśirojvaraḥ pṛcchāmi bhagavaṃs tasmāt ko bhavān iha tiṣṭhati
english: "My heart is agitated and a fever has risen in my head because of this — therefore I ask you, O blessed one: who are you who stands here?"

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca yakṣo 'ham asmi bhadraṃ te nāsmi pakṣī jalecaraḥ mayaite nihatāḥ sarve bhrātaras te mahaujasaḥ
english: The yakṣa said: "I am a yakṣa — blessings on you — I am not a water-dwelling bird. It is by me that all these brothers of yours of great energy have been slain."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tām aśivāṃ śrutvā vācaṃ sa paruṣākṣarām yakṣasya bruvato rājann upakramya tadā sthitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, having heard that terrible, harsh-syllabled speech of the yakṣa as it spoke, he advanced and stood before it.

sanskrit: virūpākṣaṃ mahākāyaṃ yakṣaṃ tālasamucchrayam jvalanārkapratīkāśam adhṛṣyaṃ parvatopamam
english: He saw the yakṣa — mis-eyed, of massive body, as tall as a palm tree, blazing like fire or the sun, unapproachable, resembling a mountain —

sanskrit: setum āśritya tiṣṭhantaṃ dadarśa bharatarṣabhaḥ meghagambhīrayā vācā tarjayantaṃ mahābalam
english: — standing perched upon a dam, that bull of the Bharatas saw it threatening him with a voice deep as a thunder-cloud, him of mighty strength.

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca ime te bhrātaro rājan vāryamāṇā mayāsakṛt balāt toyaṃ jihīrṣantas tato vai sūditā mayā
english: The yakṣa said: "These brothers of yours, O king, were stopped by me again and again, yet they tried to take the water by force — and so they were struck down by me."

sanskrit: na peyam udakaṃ rājan prāṇān iha parīpsatā pārtha mā sāhasaṃ kārṣīr mama pūrvaparigrahaḥ praśnān uktvā tu kaunteya tataḥ piba harasva ca
english: "Do not drink this water, O king, if you wish to preserve your life here. O Pārtha, do not act rashly — this is my prior possession. Answer the questions first, O son of Kuntī, then drink and take water away."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca naivāhaṃ kāmaye yakṣa tava pūrvaparigraham kāmaṃ naitat praśaṃsanti santo hi puruṣāḥ sadā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "I do not at all contest your prior possession, O yakṣa — wise men never praise such self-assertion at will."

sanskrit: yadātmanā svam ātmānaṃ praśaṃset puruṣaḥ prabho yathāprajñaṃ tu te praśnān prativakṣyāmi pṛccha mām
english: "When a man praises himself by himself, O lord, that good men do not praise. But I shall answer your questions to the best of my wisdom — ask me."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid ādityam unnayati ke ca tasyābhitaś carāḥ kaś cainam astaṃ nayati kasmiṃś ca pratitiṣṭhati
english: The yakṣa said: "What raises the sun? Who are those that move around it? What causes it to set? And in what does it abide?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brahmādityam unnayati devās tasyābhitaś carāḥ dharmaś cāstaṃ nayati ca satye ca pratitiṣṭhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Brahman raises the sun; the gods are those that move around it; dharma causes it to set; and it abides in truth."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kena svic chrotriyo bhavati kena svid vindate mahat kena dvitīyavān bhavati rājan kena ca buddhimān
english: The yakṣa said: "By what does one become learned in the scriptures? By what does one attain greatness? By what does one gain a companion, O king? And by what does one become wise?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutena śrotriyo bhavati tapasā vindate mahat dhṛtyā dvitīyavān bhavati buddhimān vṛddhasevayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "By sacred learning one becomes learned in scriptures; by austerity one attains greatness; by steadfastness one gains a companion; and one becomes wise by serving the aged."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ devatvaṃ kaś ca dharmaḥ satām iva kaś caiṣāṃ mānuṣo bhāvaḥ kim eṣām asatām iva
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the divinity of the brahmins? What is their dharma like that of the good? What is their human trait? And what is theirs that resembles the bad?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca svādhyāya eṣāṃ devatvaṃ tapa eṣāṃ satām iva maraṇaṃ mānuṣo bhāvaḥ parivādo 'satām iva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Sacred recitation is their divinity; austerity is their trait like that of the good; death is their human condition; and slander is their trait resembling the bad."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ devatvaṃ kaś ca dharmaḥ satām iva kaś caiṣāṃ mānuṣo bhāvaḥ kim eṣām asatām iva
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the divinity of the kṣatriyas? What is their dharma like that of the good? What is their human trait? And what is theirs that resembles the bad?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca iṣvastram eṣāṃ devatvaṃ yajña eṣāṃ satām iva bhayaṃ vai mānuṣo bhāvaḥ parityāgo 'satām iva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Archery and weapons are their divinity; sacrifice is their trait like that of the good; fear is truly their human condition; and abandonment of the helpless is their trait resembling the bad."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kim ekaṃ yajñiyaṃ sāma kim ekaṃ yajñiyaṃ yajuḥ kā caikā vṛścate yajñaṃ kāṃ yajño nātivartate
english: The yakṣa said: "What one Sāman is fit for sacrifice? What one Yajus is fit for sacrifice? What one thing cuts through sacrifice? And what does sacrifice not transcend?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca prāṇo vai yajñiyaṃ sāma mano vai yajñiyaṃ yajuḥ vāg ekā vṛścate yajñaṃ tāṃ yajño nātivartate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Prāṇa is the Sāman fit for sacrifice; mind is the Yajus fit for sacrifice; speech alone cuts through sacrifice; and sacrifice does not transcend speech."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid āpatatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kiṃ svin nipatatāṃ varam kiṃ svit pratiṣṭhamānānāṃ kiṃ svit pravadatāṃ varam
english: The yakṣa said: "What is best among things that fall from above? What is best among things that fall to the ground? What is best among things that stand firm? And what is best among things that speak?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca varṣam āpatatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bījaṃ nipatatāṃ varam gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhamānānāṃ putraḥ pravadatāṃ varaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Rain is best among things that fall from above; seed is best among things that fall to the ground; cows are best among things that stand firm; and a son is best among things that speak."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca indriyārthān anubhavan buddhimāṃl lokapūjitaḥ saṃmataḥ sarvabhūtānām ucchvasan ko na jīvati
english: The yakṣa said: "Who, though experiencing sense-objects, though intelligent, though honoured by the world, though regarded by all beings — who, though breathing, does not truly live?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ pitṝṇām ātmanaś ca yaḥ na nirvapati pañcānām ucchvasan na sa jīvati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "He who does not offer to the gods, to guests, to servants, to the ancestors, and to himself — he who does not serve these five — though breathing, does not truly live."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid gurutaraṃ bhūmeḥ kiṃ svid uccataraṃ ca khāt kiṃ svic chīghrataraṃ vāyoḥ kiṃ svid bahutaraṃ nṛṇām
english: The yakṣa said: "What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? And what is more numerous than grass?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mātā gurutarā bhūmeḥ pitā uccataraś ca khāt manaḥ śīghrataraṃ vāyoś cintā bahutarī nṛṇām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; and worry is more numerous among men than grass."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svit suptaṃ na nimiṣati kiṃ svij jātaṃ na copati kasya svid dhṛdayaṃ nāsti kiṃ svid vegena vardhate
english: The yakṣa said: "What does not close its eyes when asleep? What does not stir when born? What has no heart? And what grows swiftly?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca matsyaḥ supto na nimiṣaty aṇḍaṃ jātaṃ na copati aśmano hṛdayaṃ nāsti nadī vegena vardhate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "A fish does not close its eyes when asleep; an egg does not stir when born; a stone has no heart; and a river grows swiftly."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svit pravasato mitraṃ kiṃ svin mitraṃ gṛhe sataḥ āturasya ca kiṃ mitraṃ kiṃ svin mitraṃ mariṣyataḥ
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the friend of one who is abroad? What is the friend of one who stays at home? What is the friend of the sick? And what is the friend of one who is dying?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sārthaḥ pravasato mitraṃ bhāryā mitraṃ gṛhe sataḥ āturasya bhiṣaṅ mitraṃ dānaṃ mitraṃ mariṣyataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "A fellow-traveller is the friend of one abroad; a wife is the friend of one who stays at home; a physician is the friend of the sick; and charity is the friend of one who is dying."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid eko vicarati jātaḥ ko jāyate punaḥ kiṃ svid dhimasya bhaiṣajyaṃ kiṃ svid āvapanaṃ mahat
english: The yakṣa said: "What, once born, wanders alone? What is born again and again? What is the remedy for cold? And what is the great field of sowing?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sūrya eko vicarati candramā jāyate punaḥ agnir himasya bhaiṣajyaṃ bhūmir āvapanaṃ mahat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "The sun, once born, wanders alone; the moon is born again and again; fire is the remedy for cold; and the earth is the great field of sowing."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid ekapadaṃ dharmyaṃ kiṃ svid ekapadaṃ yaśaḥ kiṃ svid ekapadaṃ svargyaṃ kiṃ svid ekapadaṃ sukham
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the single word of dharma? What is the single word of fame? What is the single word of heaven? And what is the single word of happiness?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dākṣyam ekapadaṃ dharmyaṃ dānam ekapadaṃ yaśaḥ satyam ekapadaṃ svargyaṃ śīlam ekapadaṃ sukham
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Skill is the single word of dharma; generosity is the single word of fame; truth is the single word of heaven; and good conduct is the single word of happiness."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kiṃ svid ātmā manuṣyasya kiṃ svid daivakṛtaḥ sakhā upajīvanaṃ kiṃ svid asya kiṃ svid asya parāyaṇam
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the self of a man? What is his divinely-ordained friend? What is his means of livelihood? And what is his ultimate refuge?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca putra ātmā manuṣyasya bhāryā daivakṛtaḥ sakhā upajīvanaṃ ca parjanyo dānam asya parāyaṇam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "A son is the self of a man; a wife is his divinely-ordained friend; rain is his means of livelihood; and charity is his ultimate refuge."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca dhanyānām uttamaṃ kiṃ svid dhanānāṃ kiṃ svid uttamam lābhānām uttamaṃ kiṃ svit kiṃ sukhānāṃ tathottamam
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the highest among the fortunate? What is the highest among riches? What is the highest among gains? And what likewise is the highest among pleasures?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhanyānām uttamaṃ dākṣyaṃ dhanānām uttamaṃ śrutam lābhānāṃ śreṣṭham ārogyaṃ sukhānāṃ tuṣṭir uttamā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Skill is the highest among the fortunate; learning is the highest among riches; health is the best among gains; and contentment is the highest among pleasures."

sanskrit: yakṣa uvāca kaś ca dharmaḥ paro loke kaś ca dharmaḥ sadāphalaḥ kiṃ niyamya na śocanti kaiś ca saṃdhir na jīryate
english: The yakṣa said: "What is the supreme dharma in the world? What dharma always bears fruit? By restraining what do men not grieve? And with what does alliance not decay?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmas trayīdharmaḥ sadāphalaḥ mano yamya na śocanti sadbhiḥ saṃdhir na jīryate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Non-cruelty is the supreme dharma; the dharma of the three Vedas always bears fruit; by restraining the mind men do not grieve; and alliance with the good does not decay."
